reconstructed_theorem_text: Claim with a locally defined function. Let n be a positive integer, h a nonnegative integer, i an integer with 0 <= i <= h, and p an even integer satisfying 4 <= p <= Q, where Q = 2^(64(h+1)). Put m = h-i+1 (the displayed natural subtraction is truncated), B = 2^(74(h+1)), S = sum_{j=0}^{m-1} B^j, and a = 1 / [p^4 S^2 sqrt(m log(2 Q S))], with natural-number quantities interpreted as reals in this formula and log the natural logarithm. Set T = {(r,j,k) : 0 <= r < p, 0 <= j < m, 0 <= k < B^j}, and let C be the set of all functions c:T -> {0,...,n-1}. For a deterministic tuple u = (u_0,...,u_{m-1}) in (R^n)^m and a coefficient vector xi in R^C, define F(n,h,i,p,u,xi) = sqrt(n) a sum_{c in C} xi_c product_{r=0}^{p-1} product_{j=0}^{m-1} product_{k=0}^{B^j-1} (u_j)_{c(r,j,k)}. The claim is that, for every such n,h,i,p and every such u satisfying ||u_j||_2 = 1 for every j, the map xi -> F(n,h,i,p,u,xi) is almost-everywhere measurable under the standard Gaussian probability measure on R^C, and its pushforward of that measure is the real Gaussian law with mean 0 and variance max(n a^2,0), equivalently variance n a^2. Here the standard Gaussian on R^C has mean zero and identity covariance. There are p S slots and n^(p S) coefficient coordinates; u_j occurs in p B^j slots. Only xi is random. This specifies a scalar law for each fixed admissible deterministic tuple u; it does not assert a simultaneous bound, a joint law over different tuples, or a probability event uniform over u.
objects: A locally defined scalar function F with coefficient array xi; m = h-i+1; B = 2^(74(h+1)); Q = 2^(64(h+1)); S = sum_{j=0}^{m-1} B^j; a = 1/[p^4 S^2 sqrt(m log(2 Q S))]. The slot set is T = Fin p x (sum over j in Fin m of Fin(B^j)); the coefficient index set is C = (T -> Fin n). The coefficient space is EuclideanSpace R C. Each product has p S factors, of which p B^j use u_j. The source measure is the standard Gaussian on this coefficient space; the target measure is gaussianReal 0 ((n a^2).toNNReal).
domains: n in the positive natural numbers; h in the natural numbers; i in Fin(h+1), with underlying value in {0,...,h}; p a natural number in the constrained subtype Even p and 4 <= p <= 2^(64(h+1)); u:Fin m -> EuclideanSpace R (Fin n); xi in EuclideanSpace R (T -> Fin n). Every u_j has Euclidean norm 1, namely sqrt(sum_{l=0}^{n-1} (u_j)_l^2) = 1. F takes real values. The coefficient space has n^(p S) real coordinates.
quantifiers: After the local definition of F, the proposition universally quantifies n, h, i, p, u, and a proof hu of (for every j in Fin m, ||u_j|| = 1). For each fixed choice it asserts HasLaw of the coefficient-to-scalar map F(n,h,i,p,u). Its defining sum ranges over all c:T -> Fin n and its defining product over all slots (r,j,k) in T. There is no sampling or averaging of u and no existential choice of parameters or constants.
assumptions: n > 0; h >= 0; 0 <= i <= h; p even with 4 <= p <= 2^(64(h+1)); every direction u_j has Euclidean norm exactly 1. For the law assertion, the coefficient vector is distributed according to the standard Gaussian Borel probability measure on its full real Euclidean coordinate space, with mean zero and identity covariance. No orthogonality or distinctness of the directions is assumed.
conclusion: For each fixed admissible deterministic u, HasLaw asserts both AEMeasurable(F(n,h,i,p,u), stdGaussian) and Measure.map(F(n,h,i,p,u), stdGaussian) = gaussianReal(0, (n a^2).toNNReal). The variance argument is exactly max(n a^2,0) as a nonnegative real, which equals n a^2 because n is positive and a^2 is nonnegative. The conclusion is an exact one-dimensional Gaussian law, not a tail estimate, a supremum estimate, or a joint-law claim.
scopes: F is defined locally before the universal proposition. The definitions S and a inside that proposition repeat the same formulas using the universally quantified parameters. In the HasLaw assertion, only the coefficient array xi is integrated against stdGaussian; all parameters and all directions are fixed. A slot (r,j,k) uses direction u_j with coordinate c(r,j,k); repeated occurrences are retained. The universal quantifier over u gives a separate law assertion for each tuple, not a common almost-sure event over all tuples. The packet supplies no proof to reconstruct and no law for non-unit tuples.
constant_dependencies: The constants 2, 4, 64, and 74 are fixed numerals. Q and B depend only on h; m and S depend only on h and i; a depends only on h, i, and p. The prefactor sqrt(n) a and variance n a^2 depend on n, h, i, and p. Subject to the unit-norm hypothesis the asserted mean and variance do not depend on the particular direction tuple u. The coefficient index set depends on n, h, i, and p. No unspecified universal, existential, or asymptotic constants occur.
